note: No message bodies, prompts, command text or secrets in frames/structure files; drivers/commands.sh contain the trivial experiment prompts.

registry_fields.fact: claude agents --json rows: pid, cwd, kind, startedAt, sessionId, name, status, waitingFor (only when waiting). Source is $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/sessions/<pid>.json, which also has entrypoint (cli | sdk-py), messagingSocketPath, tmux, statusUpdatedAt, version.

status_values.fact: idle (interactive, no turn); busy (turn running, 0.14s after Enter); waiting + waitingFor='permission prompt' (1.6s after submit, while the terminal shows the approval dialog); back to busy 0.13s after the user answers, idle at turn end. SDK sessions (entrypoint sdk-py) also listed with kind 'interactive', and show waiting/'permission prompt' while can_use_tool is pending.

latency_to_list.fact: Not listed while the workspace-trust dialog is up; listed 0.7s after trust accepted (polling 0.5s). sessionId is present before the first prompt; after --resume the row carries the resumed sessionId.

other_profile.fact: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<other> claude agents --json returns [] while the default profile has live sessions: the registry is per config dir, so detection must run under the instance's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.
other_profile.not_verified: A live, logged-in second profile (scratch config dir is not logged in: 'Not logged in'); an unlogged interactive start under it wrote only a .key file, no row.

timely_permission_fact.fact: Yes for status: waiting/waitingFor flips within ~1.6s of the dialog appearing (registry file mtime-driven; polling cost ~0.1s per call).

transcript_as_supplement.fact: No transcript line marks a pending permission: the last line is an assistant tool_use with no tool_result (indistinguishable from a long-running tool) until the tool_result is written after the answer. Turn end writes system/turn_duration. Transcript is a weak supplement only (activity, turn end); registry is the fact source for 'waiting for approval'.

delivery_default.fact: With crossSessionInbound unset (mode parity: both prompting class) an SDK session's SendMessage was delivered; the receiver terminal started a new turn whose user line has promptSource=system, turnOrigin=peer, shown as 'Message from @<sender-name>'. The receiver answered in its own transcript; nothing came back to the sender (no reply turn within 85s) because the receiver did not SendMessage back.

sendmessage_permission.fact: SendMessage (input keys: content, message, recipient, recipient_kind, summary, to, type) ran WITHOUT can_use_tool in an SDK session with default permission mode: a Yuki-held Claude can message any same-user peer session (incl. user's own terminals) unprompted. Forcing it through can_use_tool required --settings permissions.ask=[SendMessage].

refuse.fact: Receiver transcript unchanged; the sender got a system-origin follow-up turn reporting the refusal (an extra sender turn).

hold.fact: Receiver shows 'Held peer message ... not delivered to Claude' to the user (system/informational line), no Claude turn; sender got a system-origin follow-up turn. Repo-level hold/refuse only tightens; explicit value wins over mode parity.

sender_must_be_claude.fact: No CLI subcommand sends a peer message; the documented path is the SendMessage tool, so each message costs a sender Claude turn (plus a follow-up turn on refuse/hold). The raw UDS (/tmp/cc-socks/<pid>.sock, peerProtocol 1) is undocumented and was not used.

E6.setup: Project .claude/settings.local.json stands in for the user's own allow rules: Bash(touch:*), Write/Edit(//<outside>/**). can_use_tool always denies, so 'effect happened' means the call ran without the connector being asked.

A_connector_today.fact: No permission_mode (init reports 'default'), all setting sources: user-allowed touch and write-outside ran without can_use_tool; ls ran (read-only auto-allow); mkdir and Write in cwd/add_dir reached can_use_tool.

B_acceptEdits_add_dirs_allowed_tools.fact: Writes in cwd and add_dir and mkdir in cwd ran without callback (acceptEdits also auto-allows filesystem Bash like mkdir/touch inside working dirs); user-allowed write OUTSIDE scope ran without callback -> scope bypassed.

C_setting_sources_empty.fact: User rules not loaded: write outside reached can_use_tool. (Drops user CLAUDE.md/hooks/MCP too.)

D_disallowed_tools.fact: disallowed_tools Bash(touch:*) beats user allow (denied, no callback). Write(//path/**) in disallowed did NOT match the Write tool; Edit(//path/**) did (D2: write outside denied). Path rules must use Edit(...) and '//' for absolute paths.

E_settings_ask.fact: --settings permissions.ask beats user allow: touch and (with Edit(//...)) write-outside reached can_use_tool (E2).

G_settings_ask_all.fact: --settings {permissions:{ask:[Bash,Edit,Write]}} with all user setting sources kept: EVERY Bash/Write call (incl. user-allowed touch, write-outside, read-only ls, writes in cwd) reached can_use_tool. The connector can thus enforce the delegation scope itself in the callback without dropping the user's setting sources.

E6.not_verified: Real user-level (~/.claude/settings.json) rules were not modified; project-local rules were used as stand-in (same precedence chain: flag > local > project > user, deny > ask > allow). User PreToolUse hooks that return allow, MCP tools, WebFetch, NotebookEdit were not tested. acceptEdits+ask interplay inside cwd not tested.

bg_task_notification.fact: After result+idle, ~7.3s later: system task_updated, task_notification(status=completed, task_id, tool_use_id of the owner's original Bash tool_use), background_tasks_changed, session_state_changed=running, a new system/init, assistant (parent_tool_use_id null), result(num_turns 1), session_state_changed=idle. No user/replay frame starts this turn.

stopped_then_completed.fact: TaskStop inside the same turn produced task_notification status=stopped in-turn; no later 'completed' notification and no self-started turn within 45s. The 'stopped then completed' double notification was not reproduced.

schedule_wakeup.fact: ScheduleWakeup is available headless (input keys delaySeconds, noop, prompt, reason). ~62s after the turn: session_state_changed=running, command_lifecycle=started (no preceding queued from us, no user/replay frame), system/init, assistant, result, idle.

x2_one_long_tool.fact: Foreground Bash sleep 20: tool_use at 2.4s, task_started at 5.5s (long foreground command tracked as a task), then silence (no heartbeat/progress frames) until 22.5s. Input written at 6.3s got command_lifecycle=queued immediately and was replayed (isReplay, same UUID) only at 22.5s right after the tool_result, merged into the same turn (one result).

E7.attribution_fact: Every self-started turn ran inside the SDK owner process that created the session, began with session_state_changed=running with no Yuki input outstanding, and (for background tasks) carries the originating tool_use_id.

release_at_turn_boundary.fact: SDK owner did one turn, closed at the turn boundary (process exited, no registry row). Terminal 'claude --resume <id>' displayed the SDK turn, ran its own turn; transcript is one linear chain (0 branch points; entrypoints sdk-py 14, cli 9).

resume_while_live_G8.fact: SDK resume of the same id while the terminal was live: no error, SDK result carried the same session id; terminal then ran a turn and did not see the SDK turn; transcript has 1 branch point with children [sdk-py, cli]. Before the resume the registry row of the live terminal carried that sessionId, so a pre-open check would have caught it.

fork_session.fact: resume=<id>, fork_session=True -> new session id; original transcript sha256 and line count unchanged.
